title: TOEFL Speaking 2026: Listen and Repeat & Take an Interview
summary: The two new Speaking tasks — mirroring sentences for clear pronunciation, and handling a simulated interview about your experiences and opinions.

chunks.heading: Listen and Repeat — mirror it exactly
chunks.body: You **listen to short sentences and repeat them exactly as you hear them**. It measures your ability to **process spoken English and produce accurate, clearly intelligible speech** — pronunciation, stress and rhythm.
chunks.realExample: You hear 'The seminar has been moved to Thursday afternoon' and repeat it precisely — same words, same stress on 'Thursday'. A small change like 'moved on Thursday' misses the mark.
chunks.memoryHook: Mirror it — the words, the stress, and the rhythm, all of it.

chunks.heading: Take an Interview — talk like yourself, clearly
chunks.body: You **take part in a simulated interview** about academic or campus situations, answering questions about your **experiences and opinions**. You're judged on communicating clearly, keeping a **natural pace**, and using appropriate **grammar and vocabulary**.
chunks.realExample: Asked 'Tell me about a class you enjoyed and why,' give a specific class, one clear reason, and a short example — spoken at a steady pace, not rushed or memorised-sounding.
chunks.memoryHook: Specific answer + one reason + one example, at a natural pace.

chunks.heading: Delivery beats big words
chunks.body: Both tasks reward **clear, intelligible delivery** over rare vocabulary. Slow down enough to be understood, finish your sentences, and keep a steady rhythm — clarity is what's scored.
chunks.realExample: In Listen and Repeat, resist rushing the sentence back; in the interview, a clear, well-paced everyday answer beats a fast, tangled 'impressive' one.
chunks.memoryHook: Clear and steady wins. Intelligibility over vocabulary fireworks.

recall.q: What do you do in the 'Listen and Repeat' task?
recall.a: Listen to short sentences and repeat them exactly, to show accurate, clearly intelligible speech.
Your ability to process spoken English and produce speech that is accurate and clearly intelligible — pronunciation, stress and rhythm.

recall.q: What happens in the 'Take an Interview' task?
recall.a: You answer interview questions about academic or campus experiences and opinions, judged on clarity, natural pace, grammar and vocabulary.

recall.q: What matters more than advanced vocabulary in TOEFL Speaking?
recall.a: Clear, intelligible delivery at a natural pace — being understood is what's scored.

recall.q: What is a good structure for an interview answer?
recall.a: A specific answer, one clear reason, and one short example, delivered at a steady pace.
